FakeCompanyABC Annual Leave Policy.

Purpose.

This policy defines annual paid leave, carry-forward rules, and the process for requesting leave at FakeCompanyABC.

Annual leave entitlement.

Annual leave depends on the employee's contractual work location.

Germany.

Full-time employees whose contractual work location is Germany receive 30 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year.

Pakistan.

Full-time employees whose contractual work location is Pakistan receive 24 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year.

Part-time employees receive annual leave on a pro-rata basis according to their contracted working days.

Carry-forward.

Carry-forward.

Employees may carry forward a maximum of 5 unused annual-leave days into the following calendar year.

Carried-forward leave must normally be used by 31 March of the following year. Any remaining carried-forward leave expires after that date unless HR has approved an exception in writing.

Leave requests.

Leave of 5 consecutive working days or fewer should normally be requested at least 5 working days in advance.

Leave of more than 5 consecutive working days should normally be requested at least 3 weeks in advance.

All annual-leave requests require approval from the employee's direct manager.

Probation.

All annual-leave requests require approval from the employee's direct manager.

Probation.

Employees may request annual leave during probation, but approval depends on business needs and manager approval. The annual entitlement itself is not reduced because an employee is on probation.

Important interpretation note.

The annual entitlement is based on the employee's contractual work location, not nationality, citizenship, or the country from which the employee happens to work temporarily.

Examples.

Examples.

An employee contracted in Germany with 8 unused days at year-end may carry forward only 5 days.
An employee contracted in Pakistan with 3 unused days may carry all 3 days forward.
A Germany-based employee temporarily working from Pakistan still follows the Germany annual-leave entitlement unless the employment contract is changed.

FakeCompanyABC Expense Reimbursement Policy.

Submission deadline.

Employees must normally submit business-expense claims within 30 calendar days of the expense date.

Claims submitted after 30 days require an explanation and may require additional approval.

Receipts.

A receipt is required for any individual expense above:

EUR 20 for expenses paid in euros;
PKR 6,000 for expenses paid in Pakistani rupees.

For lower-value expenses without a receipt, the employee must still provide the date, amount, and business purpose.

Meals during business travel.

The standard maximum reimbursable meal expense per person is:

Meals during business travel.

The standard maximum reimbursable meal expense per person is:

Location. Maximum per meal.
Germany. EUR 35.
Belgium. EUR 40.
Spain. EUR 35.
Pakistan. PKR 6,500.

Alcoholic beverages are not reimbursable under the standard meal allowance.

Hotels.

Hotel room-rate limits are not defined by this policy.

For hotel limits, employees must use the current Business Travel Policy, HR-TRV-0173.

This is intentional: the expense policy defines how claims are submitted, while the travel policy defines allowable hotel rates.

Ground transportation.

Reasonable public-transport expenses are reimbursable for approved business travel.

Ground transportation.

Reasonable public-transport expenses are reimbursable for approved business travel.

Taxi or ride-hailing expenses are reimbursable when public transport is impractical, unavailable, or would create an unreasonable delay. The business reason should be included in the expense claim.

Personal purchases.

Personal purchases are not reimbursable.

If a receipt contains both business and personal items, only the business portion may be claimed.

Reimbursement timing.

Approved expenses are normally reimbursed with the next available payroll cycle after finance completes review.

Examples.

Examples.

A EUR 18 taxi expense does not require a receipt under the general receipt threshold, but the business purpose must still be recorded.
A EUR 28 meal requires a receipt.
A hotel claim should be checked against HR-TRV-0173, not against the meal limits in this document.

FakeCompanyABC Parental Leave and Return-to-Work Policy.

Scope.

This document describes FakeCompanyABC's internal notification and return-to-work procedures related to parental leave.

It does not replace statutory parental-leave rights. Where local law provides a greater entitlement or different requirement, local law takes precedence.

Notification.

Employees should notify HR and their manager as early as reasonably possible when planning parental leave.

Where a specific statutory notice period applies, the statutory requirement must be followed.

Company-paid transition days.

Company-paid transition days.

In addition to any statutory entitlement, eligible full-time employees who have completed at least 12 months of continuous service may receive up to 5 company-paid transition days associated with the birth or adoption of a child.

These transition days are separate from annual leave.

Part-time employees receive transition days on a pro-rata basis.

Return-to-work arrangement.

An employee returning from parental leave may request a temporary reduced-work schedule for up to 8 weeks.

The request should normally be submitted at least 4 weeks before the planned return date.

The request should normally be submitted at least 4 weeks before the planned return date.

Approval depends on role requirements, local law, and agreement with HR and the employee's manager.

Remote work after parental leave.

Returning from parental leave does not automatically create an additional remote-work allowance.

Any remote-work arrangement must follow Remote Work Policy HR-RMT-0204 unless a specific temporary exception is approved.

Annual leave interaction.

Company-paid transition days are not deducted from the employee's annual-leave balance.

Unused annual leave remains governed by Annual Leave Policy HR-LEV-0101, including its carry-forward rules.

Examples.

Unused annual leave remains governed by Annual Leave Policy HR-LEV-0101, including its carry-forward rules.

Examples.

An eligible full-time employee with 18 months of service may receive up to 5 company-paid transition days.
An employee with only 8 months of continuous service is not eligible for the company-paid transition days under this policy, although statutory rights may still apply.
A returning employee requesting temporary remote work must also consider HR-RMT-0204.

FakeCompanyABC Remote Work Policy.

Standard remote-work allowance.

Remote-work allowances depend on contractual work location and team requirements.

Germany.

Employees contracted in Germany may normally work remotely for up to 3 days per week, subject to manager approval and team scheduling.

Employees are normally expected to work from a FakeCompanyABC office at least 2 days per week.

Pakistan.

Employees contracted in Pakistan may normally work remotely for up to 2 days per week, subject to manager approval and team scheduling.

Employees are normally expected to work from a FakeCompanyABC office at least 3 days per week.

Working from another country.

Working from another country.

Working remotely from a country other than the employee's contractual work location is not automatically covered by the normal weekly remote-work allowance.

Cross-border remote work requires prior written approval from both HR and the employee's manager because tax, immigration, payroll, information-security, and employment-law requirements may apply.

Manager approval alone is not sufficient for cross-border remote work.

Security requirements.

Employees working remotely must:

An exception to office attendance does not automatically authorize cross-border remote work.

Examples.

A Germany-based employee working from home in Germany 3 days in one week may be allowed if the manager approves.
A Pakistan-based employee normally has a maximum of 2 remote days per week.
A Germany-based employee who wants to work from Spain for one week needs HR and manager approval even if the employee has unused remote-work days.

FakeCompanyABC Business Travel Policy.

Approval.

All business travel must be approved by the employee's manager before booking.

International travel additionally requires the cost center to be identified before booking.

Air travel.

For flights with a scheduled duration of 6 hours or less, employees should book economy class.

For flights with a scheduled duration of more than 6 hours, premium economy may be booked with manager approval.

Business class requires director-level approval and a documented business justification.

Hotel limits — current policy.

The following nightly hotel limits apply from 1 January 2026:

Hotel limits — current policy.

The following nightly hotel limits apply from 1 January 2026:

Location. Maximum reimbursable room rate per night.
Germany. EUR 160.
Belgium. EUR 170.
Spain. EUR 150.
Pakistan. PKR 32,000.

The limit applies to the room rate including mandatory hotel taxes, but excluding separately charged breakfast where breakfast is reimbursable under the expense policy.

A higher rate may be reimbursed only if approved before booking by the employee's manager and the relevant cost-center owner.

Historical limits — do not use for travel from 2026 onward.

Under version 3.2, effective from 1 January 2025 through 31 December 2025, the hotel limits were:

Under version 3.2, effective from 1 January 2025 through 31 December 2025, the hotel limits were:

Location. 2025 maximum room rate per night.
Germany. EUR 130.
Belgium. EUR 145.
Spain. EUR 125.
Pakistan. PKR 26,000.

These values are retained here only for audit and historical-reference purposes.

Rail travel.

Standard class should normally be used for rail journeys under 3 hours.

First class may be used for rail journeys of 3 hours or more if the fare is reasonable and manager approval has been obtained.

Booking channels.

Employees should use the approved corporate travel provider when it is available for the destination.

Employees should use the approved corporate travel provider when it is available for the destination.

Bookings made outside the approved channel must include a short justification when the expense claim is submitted.

Exact identifier note.

This policy is identified as HR-TRV-0173. Questions referring to "TRV-0173", "HR-TRV-0173", or "travel policy 0173" refer to this policy.

Examples.

A hotel in Germany costing EUR 155 per night is within the 2026 standard limit.
A Germany hotel costing EUR 145 per night was above the standard 2025 limit but is below the 2026 limit.
A Spain hotel costing EUR 158 per night in 2026 requires advance approval because the standard limit is EUR 150.
